text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Parliament approved holding municipality elections in June for the first time since 1963.
-Austria's foreign minister Waldner, on a three-day visit to Lebanon said: "We want to strengthen our role in Lebanon and the region".
-Central bank officials will discuss today with the Lebanese Banks Association plans to cut the pound lending rate.
-The five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in south Lebanon will study today a new Lebanese complaint over the killing of a shepherd in a land mine blast.
--A military investigating judge demanded up to 10 years jail for 78 Lebanese men for allegedly collaborating with Israel.
-The General Labour Confederation will file a complaint with Arab and international labour organizations against the government for allegedly interfering in union affairs.
-Prosecutor General Addoum said information about detained Japanese Red Army suspects will be revealed as soon as investigations end.
-Parliament authorized the government to issue a 10-year $100 million eurobond and to obtain loans worth $216.3 million to help rehabilitate Lebanon's power distribution stations and build new ones.
-French Foreign Minister De Charette will visit Lebanon on March 6 during a tour to Middle East.
